scope: Literature and local-source coverage audit only. Prior scan is bounded, not all history. Priority denotes consideration, never automatic RC admission.

candidates.name: Pco / Pcodec
candidates.family: Typed numerical models and entropy-coded bins
candidates.prior: No Pco/Pcodec entry found in the bounded prior scan; CIX already has numeric deltas and planes.
candidates.upstream: Released Rust crate and wrapped API; approximate multiple modes, optional delta/lookback, entropy-coded bin plus exact offset.
candidates.publication: No first paper/release date asserted; current library and format inspected.
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 shown by upstream; transitive dependencies not audited.
candidates.contract: Preserve raw type, endianness, tails and every IEEE bit; numeric value equality alone is insufficient.
candidates.value: Potential ratio/throughput improvement on typed columns without a large neural model; not measured against CIX.
candidates.limits: Chunk training and metadata amortization matter; small or interleaved heterogeneous chunks may lose.

candidates.name: ALP
candidates.family: Decimal structure with exact exceptions
candidates.prior: Already considered in the GPU/scientific inventory; not a new discovery or integrated CIX route.
candidates.upstream: Published numerical encoding and public reference implementation.
candidates.publication: SIGMOD 2024 project; paper published in PACMMOD 2023.
candidates.license: Not independently audited here.
candidates.contract: Lossless route and exact exception stream; retain raw IEEE payload and original container.
candidates.value: Important numeric control alongside Pco, existing CIX delta/planes and generic backends.
candidates.limits: Do not confuse decimal regularity with permission to round original numbers.

candidates.name: Elf / Elf+ / Elf*, Gorilla and Chimp
candidates.family: Floating-point erasure/recovery and XOR histories
candidates.prior: No named Elf/Chimp path found in bounded scan; generic XOR/delta overlap does not establish these algorithms.
candidates.upstream: Chinese-led Elf papers and Java research code; repository includes Gorilla/Chimp controls.
candidates.publication: Elf VLDB 2023; Elf* preprint 2023.
candidates.license: No license found on inspected Elf repository landing page; unresolved for integration.
candidates.contract: Validate NaN payloads, signed zero, subnormals, infinities and exact decimal reconstruction. Harness must include tails: upstream describes dropping incomplete 1000-value test blocks.
candidates.value: A distinct decimal/XOR coding candidate, not an established CIX improvement.
candidates.limits: Java research environment and branch-specific paper behavior; native implementation and raw-bit contract unqualified.

candidates.name: zfp reversible mode
candidates.family: Block transforms and embedded bit-plane coding
candidates.prior: No zfp entry found in bounded scan. CIX spatial/lifting routes overlap conceptually, not in format or implementation.
candidates.upstream: Released C/C++ library; reversible mode explicitly supports bit-identical integer/float recovery.
candidates.publication: Reversible mode documented since v0.5.5; first release date not established here.
candidates.license: Full dependency/license audit outstanding.
candidates.contract: Use explicit reversible mode; documentation includes NaNs, infinities, subnormals and signed zeros.
candidates.value: Candidate for scientific arrays and block access; no CIX gain measured.
candidates.limits: Current documented reversible execution supports serial/OpenMP, not CUDA. Zero tolerance in another mode is not a substitute.

candidates.name: SPDP
candidates.family: Synthesized floating-point transform pipeline
candidates.prior: FPC/GFC/MPC and LC already considered; SPDP not named in bounded scan.
candidates.upstream: Author supplies standalone C compressor and HDF5-related implementation.
candidates.publication: DCC 2018 paper; author records earlier code release in 2016.
candidates.license: Embedded source license requires inspection before reuse.
candidates.contract: Binary IEEE32/64 and arbitrary retained tails; exact archive reconstruction must be qualified.
candidates.value: Lightweight control for composed numerical preprocessing beyond a single delta.
candidates.limits: Synthesis is established prior art; additional pipeline search is not automatically justified.

candidates.name: Sprintz / FIRE forecasting
candidates.family: Online prediction plus integer residual packing
candidates.priority: High as control for proposed nonlinear AR work
candidates.prior: No Sprintz entry found; CIX delta/delta2 and contexts already exist.
candidates.upstream: Research C++ implementation for multivariate integer time series.
candidates.publication: 2018 preprint and research implementation.
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 shown by upstream.
candidates.contract: Only exact original integer inputs qualify. Quantizing float/CSV inputs, discarding timestamps or normalizing text would violate CIX's contract.
candidates.value: Tests whether adaptive linear prediction explains gains attributed to a new nonlinear model.
candidates.limits: Published examples use quantized inputs and omit timestamps; their ratios cannot be imported as whole-file CIX results.

candidates.name: FSST / FSST12 / OptFSST
candidates.family: Static substring dictionaries and optimal parsing
candidates.priority: High: strings, records and SDK access
candidates.prior: No FSST entry found; CIX phrases/whole-stream dictionaries are related but not equivalent.
candidates.upstream: FSST released code; OptFSST research extension changes table construction and uses dynamic programming for a fixed table.
candidates.publication: FSST PVLDB paper; OptFSST preprint 13 July 2026, revised 26 August 2026, with public code.
candidates.license: FSST MIT; inspect OptFSST fork and dependencies before reuse.
candidates.contract: Store symbol tables, offsets and escapes. Preserve all bytes; no Unicode normalization.
candidates.value: Useful for many short strings and independently decoded fields; potential throughput benefit rather than universal best ratio.
candidates.limits: OptFSST optimizes parsing given a table, not the global compressor. Small tables/data blocks pay overhead.

candidates.name: BtrBlocks / FastLanes / Corra
candidates.family: Adaptive typed encodings, SIMD layouts and cross-column dependencies
candidates.prior: No names found in bounded scan; CIX fixed columns, record ordering and constraints already cover part of the idea.
candidates.upstream: BtrBlocks C++ library; FastLanes portable C++ format and bindings; Corra paper-level cross-column prototype.
candidates.publication: BtrBlocks and FastLanes layout 2023; Corra 2024; FastLanes file-format paper 2025.
candidates.license: BtrBlocks and FastLanes MIT shown by repositories; Corra implementation licensing not established.
candidates.contract: Typed-table round trips do not prove original CSV/JSON byte recovery. Preserve whitespace, numeric spellings, order, null representation, schema and permutation costs.
candidates.value: Candidate improvements to discovery, cross-field residuals and decode layout; not a reason to import three whole frameworks.
candidates.limits: Published analytical workloads differ from CIX archives. BtrBlocks README has conflicting platform statements; actual targets need qualification.

candidates.name: OpenZL
candidates.family: Typed compression graphs and a common decoder
candidates.prior: Already reviewed; no pinned qualified CIX adapter.
candidates.upstream: Public C/C++ library and author-reported production use, with tagged-release compatibility commitments.
candidates.publication: Paper and public release 2025; exact milestones in earlier timeline ledger.
candidates.license: BSD per upstream.
candidates.contract: A stored graph must restore original bytes; supplying format descriptions is not automatic discovery of arbitrary unknown structure.
candidates.value: Direct prior art for the architecture CIX needs; potential future graph/backend comparator.
candidates.limits: Development branch has no compatibility guarantees; not a drop-in replacement for CIX's generic recognizer.

candidates.name: CLP / Logzip
candidates.family: Template extraction, variables and structured log streams
candidates.prior: CAST/latent layout was reviewed; no CLP/Logzip entry found in bounded scan.
candidates.upstream: CLP released compression/search system for unstructured and JSON logs; Logzip clustering paper and research approach.
candidates.publication: Logzip ASE 2019; CLP OSDI 2021 and JSON work 2024.
candidates.license: CLP Apache-2.0 shown by upstream; other implementation licenses not audited.
candidates.contract: Prove original text bytes, escaping, timestamp spelling, key order and unknown-line recovery; semantic JSON equivalence is insufficient.
candidates.value: Relevant to automatic mixed structured/unstructured recognition; can supply realistic controls for template discovery.
candidates.limits: Searchable log-management systems have different goals and substantial machinery; compare representation alone before considering integration.

candidates.name: Re-Pair / MR-RePair / FOLCA / SOLCA / GCIS / GLZA
candidates.family: Recursive grammar compression and long-range repetition
candidates.prior: CIX phrase coding exists; no substantive named entries found in bounded scan after rejecting lexical false matches.
candidates.upstream: Japanese MR-RePair/SOLCA research code, GCIS author code and GLZA author paper/release posts.
candidates.publication: MR-RePair preprint 2018 / DCC 2019; GCIS DCC 2018; GLZA public work by 2016. First release dates otherwise unverified.
candidates.license: GLZA author release source carries Apache-2.0; each grammar implementation has a separate unresolved reuse audit.
candidates.contract: Pay grammar/rule coding, dictionary, order and envelope; disable any newline-removal option.
candidates.value: May capture long repeated structures beyond a bounded LZ window; compressed access and decode cost are separate benefits.
candidates.limits: Grammar node count alone is not archive size. Large working memory and slow construction can outweigh savings; do not run a tournament of all variants.

candidates.name: Kanzi
candidates.family: Modular transforms and entropy coders
candidates.prior: Newly identified by parallel last-chance review; many ingredient families already present in CIX.
candidates.upstream: Released Java/C++/Go implementations, configurable transform/coder composition and block concurrency.
candidates.publication: Release history exists; first publication/release not dated in this audit.
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 shown by upstream.
candidates.contract: Kanzi format is distinct; exact decode and block/reset costs need normal framing.
candidates.value: Useful ratio/decode-speed alternative and engineering reference; no new foundational compression principle.
candidates.limits: Do not compare its Silesia tar chart directly with CIX's separately framed member total.

candidates.name: FreeArc, Tornado, PPMd/PPMII, PPMonstr and Durilca
candidates.family: Specialist chains, LZ/PPM and context preprocessing
candidates.priority: Historical prior art; selected controls only
candidates.prior: LZ/PPM/LZP and specialist composition already covered; named implementations remain distinct.
candidates.upstream: Russian author documentation describes PPM libraries, heterogeneous-file segmentation and filter chains; FreeArc includes automatic extension-based method selection.
candidates.publication: Inspected FreeArc 0.4-era docs and Shkarin's historical release table; not current benchmark evidence.
candidates.license: Per-component licensing and present maintenance/support must be checked; not blanket integration-ready.
candidates.contract: CIX needs content validation, not copying extension-based eligibility; preserve known/unknown bytes.
candidates.value: Confirms specialist routing/segmentation and text transforms are established. PPMd can be a targeted control, not an automatic upgrade over native PPM or PAQ.
candidates.limits: Do not treat old rankings as modern records or assume fast decode from a high-ratio PPM implementation.

candidates.name: JPEG XL original-JPEG reconstruction; Lepton / Brunsli alternatives
candidates.family: Exact recoding of already-compressed JPEG
candidates.prior: Inspected CIX gray2d bridge calls JxlEncoderAddImageFrame, not JPEG reconstruction APIs. Lepton was mentioned in earlier transfer research, but untested.
candidates.upstream: libjxl AddJPEGFrame plus StoreJPEGMetadata supports original JPEG codestream reconstruction; Microsoft provides Rust Lepton; Brunsli supplies JPEG repacking.
candidates.publication: Public libraries/research implementations available; first releases not audited here.
candidates.license: Lepton Rust Apache-2.0; retained libjxl licensing already subject to RC dependency review; alternatives require their own audit.
candidates.contract: Restore JPEG bytes, metadata and any surrounding/tail bytes, not merely identical pixels. Unsupported streams must fall back.
candidates.value: Can exploit an already-retained codec library beyond raw grayscale images; no local savings measured.
candidates.limits: Capability opportunity is not a current restoration obligation unless previously promised; native bridge, resource bounds and full-file byte parity remain needed.

candidates.name: Precomp / preflate / compressed-stream reconstruction
candidates.family: Rebuild a known encoder and code decision residuals
candidates.priority: Preserve closed dispositions and existing PAQ route
candidates.prior: Extensively reviewed and tested in finite gzip/bzip2/ZIP closure; useful existing PAQ DEFLATE capability retained.
candidates.upstream: Released Precomp supports exact reconstruction of several compressed stream types with reconstruction data.
candidates.publication: Public C++ releases; inspected repository lists 0.4.7 in 2019.
candidates.license: Precomp Apache-2.0 with multiple bundled dependency licenses.
candidates.contract: All original syntax and compressed bytes must be recovered; ordinary decompress/recompress is insufficient.
candidates.value: Strong prior art for residual-on-generator ideas; broader media coverage remains separate from gzip evidence.
candidates.limits: Current review does not reopen rejected fixed gzip/ZIP routes or promote paid gzip/bzip2 prototypes.

candidates.name: WavPack / FLAC
candidates.family: Audio prediction, channel decorrelation and residual coding
candidates.prior: Prediction overlaps CIX/PAQ; no dedicated WavPack route found. FLAC is prior art in constraint-lifting review.
candidates.upstream: Released libraries and applications. WavPack documents default preservation of original headers/metadata; FLAC has RFC specification.
candidates.publication: Mature releases; FLAC RFC 9639 published 2024.
candidates.license: Pin library and application licenses separately before integration.
candidates.contract: Use lossless mode and preserve container bytes; float-to-integer conversion is not lossless. FLAC sample exactness alone is not original WAV byte exactness.
candidates.value: Plausible specialist for genuine audio regions, potentially with much cheaper decode than generic high-effort modelling.
candidates.limits: No representative CIX evidence; parsing, tails, channel layout and malformed input must be covered.

candidates.name: SPRING and genomic specialists
candidates.family: Sequence redundancy plus separately coded qualities/identifiers
candidates.priority: Low until a relevant input class exists
candidates.prior: Generic byte/chemical graph models do not establish FASTQ-specific coding.
candidates.upstream: Research implementation and distributed software with lossless and lossy options.
candidates.publication: Public paper/code; precise first release not checked.
candidates.license: Dependency/license review not completed.
candidates.contract: Retain identifiers, qualities, read order, lexical details and full source envelope. FASTQ.gz input support does not establish original gzip-byte reconstruction.
candidates.value: Worth considering for genomic workloads; not a reason to acquire a new corpus now.
candidates.limits: Large memory/temp costs and lossy/reordering flags require explicit exclusion or invertible side data.

candidates.name: FastCDC / similarity grouping / DwarFS
candidates.family: Cross-file deduplication and long-range shared content
candidates.priority: High for archive/filesystem design; conditional for single files
candidates.prior: No FastCDC/DwarFS entry found in bounded scan; local LZ or record ordering is not the same capability.
candidates.upstream: FastCDC paper; released DwarFS groups similar content, segments files and uses existing codecs.
candidates.publication: FastCDC USENIX ATC 2016; DwarFS released application, first date not audited.
candidates.license: DwarFS and any chosen CDC implementation need separate license/embedding review.
candidates.contract: Hash is a lookup accelerator, not proof of equality. Confirm bytes; charge reference/chunk/permutation metadata and make every referenced byte available to decoding.
candidates.value: Potentially large benefit on redundant archives/snapshots even when individual streams are compressed.
candidates.limits: Different scope from one-file codec records. Random access, bounded indexing and total storage including dictionaries/references matter.

candidates.name: G-ALP
candidates.family: Data-parallel floating-point decode
candidates.priority: Correct prior GPU inventory; conditional accelerator
candidates.prior: ALP already considered, but earlier review did not establish GPU implementation. This supplies specific paper/code evidence.
candidates.upstream: GPU-optimized ALP with parallel exception patching and decoding designed for consuming GPU kernels; linked implementation in FastLanes.
candidates.publication: DaMoN 2025; CWI records 23 June 2025.
candidates.license: FastLanes repository MIT; exact selected component/dependencies still need pinning.
candidates.contract: Lossless numeric payload plus CPU decoder compatibility and exact original-byte envelope must be established locally.
candidates.value: Potential device-resident decode/processing benefit; not a demonstrated CIX host-to-host speedup.
candidates.limits: Published GPU hardware differs from local GTX1650. FastLanes still labels its broader CUDA reader coming soon; G-ALP code is not complete reader qualification.

candidates.name: SLEEK lossless
candidates.family: High-throughput floating-point memory compression
candidates.prior: No substantive SLEEK entry found in bounded scan; related LC/FPC/GFC/MPC already considered.
candidates.upstream: 2026 CPU/GPU research code with separate lossless and lossy paths; authors claim identical cross-device compressed and restored outputs.
candidates.publication: IPDPS May 2026 paper and public source.
candidates.license: BSD-3-Clause shown in upstream source header; full component audit outstanding.
candidates.contract: Choose lossless path only; author documentation includes IEEE special values. Verify raw bits locally, including NaN payloads.
candidates.value: Plausible transfer/memory-throughput candidate; no measured CIX benefit or current-host qualification.
candidates.limits: Author measurements use CUDA12 and other GPUs; PCI transfers, 4GiB VRAM, alignment, tails and total workspace matter.

candidates.name: Existing GPU and component frameworks: libcubwt, nvCOMP, ndzip, LC, GPULZ, GFC/MPC, dietGPU, hipCOMP
candidates.family: Parallel implementations and specialized numerical streams
candidates.prior: Detailed earlier GPU audit and unexecuted libcubwt probe specification exist.
candidates.upstream: Multiple public implementations/provider distributions, with differing wire formats, licenses and CPU fallback guarantees.
candidates.publication: See existing GPU source ledger; not newly dated here.
candidates.license: Provider-specific; nvCOMP distribution differs from open-source research components.
candidates.contract: Exact CPU/GPU interoperability and emitted format must be explicit; ANS entropy stage does not make a preceding lossy transform exact.
candidates.value: Acceleration opportunity remains conditional, not exhausted by negative CPU composition experiments.
candidates.limits: No CIX GPU speedup or provider acceptance follows from availability; G-ALP/SLEEK supplement rather than erase the existing audit.

candidates.name: ZipNN / DFloat11
candidates.family: Exact compression of model-weight bit fields
candidates.prior: No names found in bounded scan; existing planes/histograms are related mechanisms.
candidates.upstream: Published research and public implementations aimed at model storage/inference; numerical bit fields have nonuniform statistics.
candidates.publication: ZipNN preprint 2024; DFloat11 preprint / NeurIPS 2025.
candidates.license: Per-component and model packaging licenses not audited here.
candidates.contract: Compress existing original weights exactly; quantization to create easier weights is a separate lossy operation.
candidates.value: A realistic application of type-aware entropy coding for BF16/FP32 tensors.
candidates.limits: CIX already has related transforms; must show marginal value. Inference-framework and large-GPU speed claims do not transfer to this server.

candidates.name: ts_zip, LMCompress, LLMZip and Language Modeling is Compression
candidates.family: Large pretrained probability models plus entropy coding
candidates.priority: Research frontier, not current RC dependency
candidates.prior: NNCP/LibNC and PAQ neural variants already considered; these are distinct larger-model approaches.
candidates.upstream: ts_zip distributes experimental binaries; DeepMind provides research code. LMCompress paper found, but separate complete releasable implementation not verified here.
candidates.publication: LLMZip 2023; DeepMind ICLR 2024; LMCompress 2024 preprint; ts_zip observed 2024 distribution.
candidates.license: Each implementation, runtime and model asset needs its own rights/dependency check.
candidates.contract: Pin tokenizer, weights, deterministic arithmetic and model identity; charge corpus-derived assets and report shared model footprint.
candidates.value: Stronger prediction can improve selected data classes; no general dominance established by headline paper ratios.
candidates.limits: Current ts_zip page explicitly claims cross-hardware deterministic inference, correcting older same-GPU caveats. Still experimental, no backward-compatibility promise, and local memory/speed unqualified.

candidates.name: Rice-Marlin / variable-to-fixed coding
candidates.family: Dictionary-based entropy coding with fast decoding
candidates.prior: Huffman/range/ANS already covered; variable-to-fixed dictionaries are not identical to combinatorial rank.
candidates.upstream: Research proposes compact dictionary constructions; public release qualification not established in this audit.
candidates.publication: Rice-Marlin preprint 2018; related Marlin DCC 2017.
candidates.license: Implementation/license unresolved.
candidates.contract: Pay dictionary/model selection and final partial codeword; compare same normalized symbol source.
candidates.value: Possible throughput/overhead trade-off, not new data prediction or a promised ratio win.
candidates.limits: No profiled CIX entropy bottleneck or decisive advantage demonstrated; do not reopen the closed standalone-coder programme automatically.

candidates.name: Near-lossless ELF; quantized SZ/cuSZ/SZx; semantic or perceptual compression
candidates.family: Excluded or carefully separated non-byte-exact modes
candidates.prior: Lossy scientific paths already excluded; this review adds a concrete ELF name collision.
candidates.upstream: ds2-lab ELF explicitly describes near-lossless model-weight transformation, unlike Spatio-Temporal-Lab Elf.
candidates.publication: ELF VLDB 2024 project; SZ family ongoing.
candidates.license: Not material to the exactness rejection.
candidates.contract: Small numerical error, same model accuracy, identical appearance or semantic equivalence is not original-byte reconstruction.
candidates.value: Their predictors may inspire exact-residual research, but reported lossy ratios cannot support CIX claims.
candidates.limits: Do not blanket-exclude a package that has a separate proven exact mode. zfp reversible qualifies for consideration; documented SZ3 lossless passthrough is ordinary Zstd, not a new transform.

candidates.name: Chinese APCF preprint
candidates.family: Floating-point precision/erasure-style preprocessing lead
candidates.prior: Not found in inspected inventory.
candidates.upstream: Native-language author preprint listing located; full page retrieval failed, so exactness and implementation could not be audited.
candidates.publication: 中国科技论文在线 listing dated 23 April 2025.
candidates.license: No code/reuse status established.
candidates.contract: Need original paper/code to verify whether every original IEEE bit is reconstructed.
candidates.value: A discoverability lead only; numerical improvements in the listing are unverified author claims.
candidates.limits: Do not rank or recommend implementation from a search snippet.
